calls.headline: No warnings are in force. Monday turns very mild and wet, Tuesday brings a squally gale (gusts about 75-90 km/h around midday), and a strong, dry high then takes over from Thursday into early November. Meanwhile the polar vortex heads for record weakness, with roughly even odds of a brief reversal around 3-10 Nov.

A Met Office yellow wind warning covers Edinburgh from 03:00 to 21:00 on Tuesday 27 Oct, with gusts of 65-80 km/h; the airport was already gusting 65 km/h before 23:00. From Thursday a strong high brings a long, dry, calm and often foggy spell to about 8 November. Meanwhile the polar vortex weakens far below its record low for the date, with about a 35-50% chance of a brief reversal around 4-10 Nov.

A Met Office yellow wind warning runs until 21:00 today, with gusts near 80 km/h. High pressure then brings a mostly dry, calm and often foggy spell from Thursday to about 7 November. Meanwhile most ensembles now reverse the polar vortex briefly around 4-9 November.

No warnings are in force. After a mild, mostly dry end to October, a very strong high (about 1040 hPa over Scotland) brings a dry, calm and often foggy spell with chilly nights from 2 to about 7 November. Above it, nearly every physics ensemble now reverses the polar vortex around 4-10 November.

No warnings are in force. It stays dry and mild to Halloween, then a strong high brings fog and chilly nights from 2 November. The polar vortex is now all but certain to reverse around 4-10 November, which raises the odds of colder, blocked spells from mid-November.

No warnings are in force. Halloween stays dry and mild, then a strong high brings fog, grey days and a chilly night into Monday 2 November. Rain returns from about 8-9 November. Meanwhile the polar vortex reverses around 4-5 November in every ECMWF and Canadian ensemble member.

No warnings are in force. Halloween stays dry and mild, then a strong high over Scotland brings a week of calm, foggy, grey weather, with rain returning around 9-10 November. Overhead, the polar vortex is forecast to reverse around 5 November in every ECMWF and Canadian ensemble member.

No warnings are in force. High pressure keeps Edinburgh dry, calm and often foggy up to Bonfire Night, then it turns greyer and damper from 6-7 November and wetter from about 10 November. Overhead, the polar vortex reverses to easterly from about 5 November in every ECMWF, GEFS and Canadian ensemble member.

No warnings are in force. Edinburgh stays dry under a 1042 hPa high, with frosty, foggy mornings (the airport fell to -1 °C overnight) and a little drizzle on Tuesday. It turns greyer and damper from 6-7 November and wetter and windier from about 10 November. Overhead, the polar vortex reverses to easterly from about 5 November in every ECMWF and GEFS ensemble member.
Quiet and dry under high pressure to Thursday, grey and damp at times from Friday, then a possible cold northerly on 11-13 November.
A frosty, foggy start, then grey with light rain at times, and a cold northerly is now more likely on 12-14 November.
Grey and mild to Sunday with light rain at times, then a cold northerly with frost is likely on 12-14 November, but GFS stays mild.
Grey and mild to Sunday, rain is likely on Wednesday 11 November, and then all main models bring a frosty northerly on 12-14 November.
Grey and mostly dry to Tuesday, rain on Wednesday 11 November is now uncertain, and a clear, frosty northerly spell follows on 12-14 November.
Light rain clears by midday, then mostly dry weather to Wednesday, a frosty northerly on 12-14 November, and heavy rain and strong winds from 16 November.
Dry and cold to 14 November, with frost likely on the nights of 11-13 November, then Atlantic rain and strong winds from 15 November.
Dry with frost to 14 November, then rain and gales from 15 November. High above us, a record-early major SSW peaks on 11-12 November.
Frost on the next two mornings and rain on 15 November come first. A cold, showery trough then gives ice and hill snow on 16-19 November, after the record-early major SSW ends on 13 November.
Frost tonight and rain on Sunday 15 November come first, then a cold, showery week brings ice in the city and snow on the Pentlands.
Rain on Sunday 15 November brings ice on Monday morning. A wetter front on Tuesday 17 November starts as snow on the Pentlands. An easterly with showers follows on 19 November.
